text.p: In a revitalised stock market, the FTSE 100 index should march ahead towards 4,690-4,700 on Monday, technical analysts said.

There should now be sufficient momentum for the index --following its 68.8 advance on Friday -- for market bulls to come out fighting and it will be a measure of investor confidence that the index can quickly re-establish the uptrend which it seemed to have lost since mid-May, they added.
The market has broken above its 10-day moving average -- now at 4,621 -- and this reinforces the bull case.
By 0740 GMT, the FTSE was up 21.9 at 4,666.9.

The comprehensive manner by which the Dow Jones industrial average smashed above a descending trendline on Friday -- which connects its intra-day highs for the previous eight days -- and closing at a record high, implies further gains for U.S. equities and this should be positive for U.K. stocks, analysts said.
On Friday, the Dow closed up 130.49 points at 7,435.78.
